root_cause.text: The `load_segments()` function in the kexec code path modifies segment registers, which invalidates the GS base register that KCOV instrumentation depends on for accessing per-CPU data, causing subsequent instrumented code to crash in an endless loop.
root_cause.evidence: The patch disables KCOV instrumentation for `machine_kexec_64.o` and `physaddr.o` with an explicit comment stating "load_segments() invalidates the GS base, which KCOV relies on for per-CPU data." The CVE description confirms that after `load_segments()` executes, any subsequent instrumented C code call (such as `native_gdt_invalidate()`) crashes the kernel because KCOV's fast-path (`__sanitizer_cov_trace_pc()`) can no longer access its per-CPU coverage data through the now-invalid GS base.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable KCOV instrumentation for machine_kexec_64.o to prevent crashes during kexec when load_segments() invalidates the GS base that KCOV relies on.
intent_record.what: Added a 16-line comment block explaining the rationale for disabling KCOV instrumentation, followed by a new Makefile variable assignment `KCOV_INSTRUMENT_machine_kexec_64.o := n` to disable KCOV for the machine_kexec_64.o object file.
intent_record.how: This change prevents the KCOV (kernel code coverage) instrumentation tool from instrumenting the machine_kexec_64.o file. At runtime, this avoids crashes that occur during kexec operations because load_segments() invalidates the GS base register that KCOV depends on for per-CPU data access. By disabling KCOV for this specific file, the kexec functionality can execute safely without KCOV instrumentation overhead or crashes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable KCOV instrumentation for physaddr.o to prevent coverage tracking issues in this kernel module, consistent with existing instrumentation exclusions.
intent_record.what: Added two lines to arch/x86/kernel/Makefile: a comment referencing the 'Disable KCOV' section and a new KCOV_INSTRUMENT_physaddr.o := n directive to disable KCOV instrumentation for the physaddr.o object file.
intent_record.how: This change prevents the KCOV (kernel code coverage) instrumentation tool from instrumenting the physaddr.o compilation unit. KCOV instrumentation adds runtime coverage tracking code, which can cause issues in certain kernel modules. By disabling it for physaddr.o, the build system ensures this object file is compiled without coverage instrumentation, similar to other sensitive kernel modules already listed above it.
